To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new spatial motion smoothing algorithm for pixel domain DVC.
the performance of the Wyner-Ziv codec can be significantly improved by using better motion compensated interpolated frames.
we propose a new motion compensated frame interpolation algorithm that allows significant improvements in RD performance of a pixel domain DVC system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) a novel spatial smoothing technique that improves the performance of motion compensated frame interpolation (MCFI); (2) a novel MCFI technique that uses a combination of spatial and temporal information; (3) a novel distributed video codec based on the pixel domain Wyner-Ziv coding that uses a combination between MCFI and the spatially-smoothed MCFI.

the design of a pixel domain Wyner-Ziv codec with the following characteristics: (i) low complexity encoder, (ii) low complexity decoder, (iii) high coding efficiency, (iv) robustness to transmission errors, (v) scalability.
the development of a new motion compensation algorithm to improve the RD performance of pixel domain DVC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed spatial motion smoothing algorithm is able to improve the quality of interpolated frames and, consequently, the RD performance of the DVC scheme.
the proposed spatial motion smoothing algorithm for pixel domain DVC is a simple, effective and efficient solution for improving the performance of DVC systems.
the proposed algorithm is a very promising solution for DVC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed spatial motion smoothing method is able to improve the RD performance by up to 0.7 dB for the same bit rate and by up to 1.2 dB for the same PSNR.
the use of motion compensated frame interpolation in the decoder is a very promising approach for the improvement of the performance of pixel domain distributed video codecs.
the proposed spatial motion smoothing algorithm is able to improve the quality of the side information and therefore the performance of the DVC scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in pixel domain DVC, the use of motion compensation based frame interpolation algorithms is an effective way to improve the RD performance.
frame interpolation can be used to improve the performance of DVC, without requiring the encoder to perform motion estimation/compensated.
, by using spatial motion smoothing, the RD performance of a pixel domain DVC can be significantly improved.
